_comment: AS-28 (closure + image, D34). AEGIS SaaS defense-image closure deny list + manifest. Generated from framework.v2.aegis.closure; test_saas_closure.py::test_closure_manifest_matches_module asserts no drift. The analyzer is SOUND against PEP 562 lazy re-exports (it follows verify/__init__'s __getattr__ + _LAZY_SYMBOLS/_SUBMODULES map, fail-closed on an opaque shim) and against a lazy/function-local offense import smuggled into an AEGIS serving module (a conservative overlay scans every reachable framework.v2.aegis module's full source — catching the literal, PEP 562 lazy-re-export AND dynamic-string importlib/__import__ forms, fail-closed on an opaque shim). A runtime probe (import the entrypoints with the agent SDKs blocked, assert no is_denied module in sys.modules) is the robust backstop. Honest scope: this proves NO DENIED module is import-reachable; the agent-executor residual below IS loaded and is disclosed, not claimed absent. The in-CI image build/scan/SBOM/sign is DEFERRED to the owner-gated A14 leg.
known_residual_note: Offense agent-executor host modules (framework.v2.agents.*) still IMPORT-reachable (and so loaded in the serving process) via the EAGER intel/__init__ -> planner/__init__ -> agents/__init__ chain (agents.blackboard/coordinator from planner.planner; agents.tools from aegis.sensors). This is DISCLOSED, never claimed absent. Closing it is the same lazy-package move as the AS-28 verify fix, applied to offense-core packages OUTSIDE the AS-28 VERIFY-token lane and requiring a make-gate byte-identity re-baseline. Deferred to the companion GW/engine-core decoupling; ratcheted (must shrink, never grow).

soundness.pep562_lazy_reexport: The walk reads a package __init__'s module-level __getattr__ + _LAZY_SYMBOLS/_SUBMODULES string-literal maps and follows each lazily re-exported from-name to its real submodule (so `from framework.v2.verify import OOBReceiver` is seen to reach the denied framework.v2.verify.oob). Fail-closed on an opaque/unparseable shim.
soundness.serving_lazy_offense_overlay: Besides the module-level import closure, every reachable framework.v2.aegis serving module's FULL source (module scope AND function/method bodies, excluding if TYPE_CHECKING:) is scanned; a lazy/function-local offense import there fails the gate. The overlay is as strong as the module-level walk: it resolves a LITERAL `from ..verify.oob import X`, a PEP 562 lazy re-export (`from framework.v2.verify import OOBReceiver` -> the denied verify.oob; fail-closed on an opaque __getattr__ shim), AND a dynamic-string `importlib.import_module("framework.v2.verify.oob")` / `__import__("...")` — so none of those forms can smuggle a denied module into a serving function body past the gate. Scoped to the AEGIS-owned serving layer: the shared verify/agents engine code legitimately reaches offense at INVOKE time, governed by the runtime probe.
soundness.runtime_probe: test_saas_closure.py imports the entrypoints in a subprocess with the LLM/agent SDKs made unimportable, then asserts no closure.is_denied module (first-party offense OR third-party SDK) is in sys.modules. Non-vacuous (negative control loads a denied module and confirms detection).
soundness.oob_relocation: The gateway's former lazy `from ..verify.oob import OOBReceiver` (a DENIED module) was removed: the neutral loopback-only receiver primitive now lives in framework.v2.common.oob_receiver (offense-free shared infra), verify.oob is a thin re-export (still denied; offense-only), and the AEGIS passive OOB canary correlator imports the common primitive. The defense serve path no longer references the denied verify.* offense namespace, lazily or eagerly.
